findings.title: An aborted worker that never entered Native makes post-join cleanup permanently pending
findings.trigger: The created worker has not entered REENTRY_RUN_CANCEL when main reaches failure cleanup. One reachable schedule is that the worker is delayed past the four-second Cocoa wait: the callback times out, the uncancelled install completes or exceeds main's elapsed bound, and main reaches done and executes REENTRY_ABORT before the worker's Native entry.
source_trace: REENTRY_ABORT sets aborted=TRUE. The subsequently scheduled worker takes the reentry_run_cancel early return at native lines115-116, before setting worker_started, worker_done or the admitted-CANCEL flag.

Main's join_worker can then successfully observe kernel thread termination. The client nevertheless unconditionally requires REENTRY_SYNC_SEQUENCE whenever the worker handle exists and joined is true.
reentry_sync_sequence requires reentry.worker_done. That flag remains false forever for this aborted-before-entry worker, so SYNC returns ERROR_IO_PENDING and the client changes cleanup to FALSE.

The following LIVE_CLEANUP and FINISH calls are gated by cleanup and are skipped. This can retain an actual uncancelled installed model, exported context, RO owners, observation refs, windows and handles until outer process cleanup, despite the worker having been joined.
findings.evidence_boundary: The client truthfully emits cleanup=false and fails the run; this is a reachable failure-cleanup leak/progress defect, not a fabricated successful-run result. The scheduling scenario was not executed.
findings.requested_change: After actual kernel join, distinguish whether the ordinary CANCEL was admitted. If it was not admitted, do not require a worker_done-gated sequence sync or advance bookkeeping as though CANCEL consumed a sequence; continue ordinary LIVE_CLEANUP and FINISH. Alternatively make aborted-before-start termination explicitly observable and safely handled by the post-join synchronization path. Keep cleanup gated on unresolved live activity, not on a terminal worker state that this early-return path can never publish.

findings.title: Gate timeout/failure exits before Native and makes post-join cleanup wait on an impossible worker_done
findings.trigger: The new worker's WaitForSingleObject(entry_gate,5000) returns WAIT_TIMEOUT or WAIT_FAILED before main successfully releases the gate. A timeout is reachable if main is delayed before SetEvent; the wait is explicitly finite and the preceding operations/output have no hard aggregate deadline.
source_trace: abort-client.c:98 sets worker_status=STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL and returns without invoking REENTRY_RUN_CANCEL. Native worker_started and worker_done both remain false, so the new Native after-ABORT branch is never entered.
Main detects the failed worker result at line157, or reaches failure cleanup earlier. Its kernel join can still succeed and joined becomes true.
Failure cleanup nevertheless requires REENTRY_SYNC_SEQUENCE whenever worker_handle exists and joined is true, without distinguishing a thread that never entered Native.
SYNC at reentry-native.inc:156 still requires reentry.worker_done. That flag cannot become true after this worker has already exited without Native entry, so SYNC returns ERROR_IO_PENDING.

The client sets cleanup=false and skips ordinary LIVE_CLEANUP and FINISH at lines188-189. The real context, reserved host/RO owners, observation refs, windows and handles can remain owned until external process cleanup even though the sole worker is already joined and no CANCEL/import was admitted.
findings.evidence_boundary: This does not fake a successful run: failures/cleanup=false are reported. It is an unnecessary failure-cleanup leak/progress defect in a reachable gate-error path. The successful gated ABORT schedule is otherwise sound. No timeout or runtime scenario was executed by this reviewer.
findings.requested_change: Record whether this PE worker actually invoked Native, publish that fact through the real kernel join, and skip the worker_done-gated sequence sync when it never entered Native. With ABORT complete and the worker joined, perform ordinary LIVE_CLEANUP and FINISH without consuming the unused CANCEL sequence. Alternatively arrange that the gate-error path safely enters the now-aborted Native RUN before exiting. Retain resources only for genuinely unresolved live activity.
